question: Foetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD) is estimated to affect millions of European citizens and Europe has been identified as having the highest prevalence of FASD globally. In the light of this: 1.
What action is the Commission taking to support greater recognition of FASD across Member States and to promote more consistent approaches to diagnosis, data collection and prevalence monitoring?

How is the Commission supporting the inclusion of people living with FASD within the objectives of the European Disability Rights Strategy 2021–2030 and the implementation of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, including access to appropriate health, education, employment, disability and social supports?

Does the Commission intend to consider further EU-level guidance or policy measures, including the explicit recognition of FASD within future disability and public health initiatives, to address inequalities in the recognition of and support for people living with FASD across the EU?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.9.2026) Foetal alcohol spectrum disorder is classified as rare disease (ORPHA 1915).

Since 2017, the Commission has been funding the European Reference Networks for Rare Diseases (ERNs), which enable specialists in Europe to discuss cases of patients affected by rare, lowprevalence and complex diseases, providing advice on the most appropriate diagnosis and the best treatment available.

Foetal alcohol spectrum disorder in particular is covered by the ERN for Rare Malformation Syndromes and Rare Intellectual and Neurodevelopmental Disorders (ITHACA). The Strategy for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities 2021-2023 further supports selfdetermination, autonomy and participation. It covers persons with different kinds of disabilities equally.

Rare diseases often lead to disabilities and thus the Strategy in its health area focuses on fostering research and innovation on rare diseases. The Pharma Package also intends to make orphan drugs against rare diseases more accessible1. The Commission is currently implementing the current actions of the Strategy.

On different occasions, including the meetings of the Disability Platform, it discusses progress on implementation, which can help define new needs to be integrated into the Strategy and feed into future policy measures.
